summary: Describes LEX, a Uniform Resource Name namespace for naming persistent resources in the legal domain, such as laws and court decisions. It lets multiple jurisdictions adopt a common convention for referencing them. It is an Independent Submission.

eli5.summary: Every law or court decision can get a permanent name tag in a shared style, so it can be found even if the web page it lived on moves.

questions: how does lex identify legal documents across jurisdictions
what is a lex urn name
subtitle: A standard way to name legal documents so they can be found anywhere.

tldr.problem: Laws, court decisions and regulations are stored in different places with different naming systems, making it hard to cite them consistently.
tldr.mechanism: LEX is a URN namespace that assigns a persistent, location-independent name to any legal document based on its content and source, with a structure that captures jurisdiction, authority, document type, date and number.
tldr.outcome: Legal documents can be referenced uniformly across jurisdictions and systems, enabling interoperability among legal information systems.

today: RFC 9676 is an active Informational RFC. The LEX namespace is registered in the Formal URN Namespaces registry. IANA has delegated the LEX namespace to CNR, which maintains the jurisdiction code registry and root resolution server at lex-nameserver.nic.it. The RFC has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: The Problem and the Solution
sections.content:
Legal documents—laws, court decisions, regulations, and administrative acts—are published by thousands of authorities across the world. Each jurisdiction manages its own legal information, and while some publish online, their systems do not talk to each other. There is no standard way to refer to a law from Italy to a judge in France, or to cite a Brazilian court decision in an international treaty. LEX solves this by providing a persistent identifier that describes the document itself, not where it is stored.

LEX stands for a Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace, which means it is a stable, location-independent naming scheme for resources. Unlike URLs, which point to a specific web address, a URN like urn:lex:it:stato:legge:2006-05-14;22 says "this is an Italian state law from May 14, 2006, number 22." The document's location can change, but its LEX name stays the same. This enables automated resolution—a legal database can look up the document by its LEX name and direct users to wherever it is currently published.
sections.eli5: A law is like a person: it has a fixed identity separate from where you can find them. LEX names give laws a permanent ID card so lawyers and judges worldwide can refer to the same law the same way, no matter which website publishes it.

sections.title: How LEX Names Are Built
sections.content:
Every LEX name has a hierarchical structure that captures the essence of the legal document. The format is:

urn:lex:jurisdiction:authority:measure:details[:annex][@expression][$manifestation]

Breaking this down:

  • Jurisdiction: The country or international organization (e.g., it for Italy, eu for the European Union). It typically uses the country's internet domain code.
  • Authority: Who issued the document (e.g., the state, a ministry, a court). Authority can be hierarchical (e.g., ministry.justice;department.penitentiary).
  • Measure: The type of document (e.g., legge for Italian laws, decision for court decisions). May include specializations like act;bankruptcy.
  • Details: The date (in ISO 8601 format like 2006-05-14) and the document's official number. Multiple dates or numbers are separated by commas.
  • Annex (optional): If the document has formal annexes, each gets its own identifier.
  • Expression (optional): Information about versions (when the law was amended) and the language it is written in.
  • Manifestation (optional): Information about the format (PDF, XML, HTML) and publisher.

For example, urn:lex:ch;glarus:regiere:erlass:2007-10-15;963 identifies a decree (erlass) issued by the government (regiere) of the Glarus canton in Switzerland on October 15, 2007, with number 963.
sections.eli5: A LEX name is like a legal document's full mailing address: country, the office that made it, what kind of document, when it was issued, and its number. Everything you need to find the exact document.

sections.title: The Four Levels: Work, Expression, Manifestation
sections.content:
LEX follows a model called FRBR (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records), which divides any intellectual creation into four levels:

  • Work: The abstract legal document itself. A law from 1941 is still "the same work" even after amendments. The authority, measure type, date and number define the work.
  • Expression: A specific version of the work. The original version of a law and the version after it was amended in 1998 are different expressions. Language differences also create different expressions. Expressions are identified by adding an amendment date and language code (e.g., @1998-02-19:fr for the French version updated in 1998).
  • Manifestation: A specific publication format. The same law might exist as an XML file from the parliament, a PDF from the senate, or an HTML document on a website. Each is a different manifestation. Manifestations are identified by adding publisher, format, and component information (e.g., $parlamento.it:application-pdf).

This model allows the same legal document to have multiple identifiers reflecting its different versions and formats, while the work identifier remains stable. A legal citation need only use the work level, but systems can track and link to specific versions and formats when needed.
sections.eli5: A law is like a book: the book itself is the work; a translated edition is an expression; a specific paperback copy is a manifestation. LEX can name the book, or any version, or any copy separately.

sections.title: Who Maintains LEX Names
sections.content:
LEX is maintained by a distributed governance structure. The National Research Council of Italy (CNR) maintains the root registry and manages the jurisdiction codes. Each country or organization that adopts LEX appoints a Jurisdictional Registrar responsible for:

  • Defining the structure of the authority and measure elements for that jurisdiction
  • Establishing rules for assigning LEX names consistently
  • Maintaining registries of authorities and measure types
  • Ensuring all assigned LEX names are unique

The jurisdiction code itself is based on the country's internet domain (ccTLD for countries, or domain name for international organizations). For example, Brazil's code is br, the EU's is eu, and the United Nations would be un.org. Jurisdiction codes are permanent and never deleted; they can only be marked obsolete if no longer used for new assignments.

A distributed resolution system maps LEX names to actual documents. The system uses DNS and NAPTR records to route queries to the appropriate jurisdiction's resolver, which then returns the document's location or the document itself.
sections.eli5: Italy's government maintains the master list. Each country keeps its own list of which numbers mean what. When you want to find a law, you ask the Italian master server, which directs you to the right country, which directs you to the actual document.

sections.title: Finding and Using LEX Names
sections.content:
LEX names are designed to be used in references, links, and citations. A legal document can embed its LEX name in metadata—either within the document itself (as an XML element or HTML meta tag) or externally (in a database or as linked data). This makes it possible for parsers to extract references from legal texts and automatically resolve them.

When a LEX name needs to reference a specific part of a document (such as paragraph 3 of article 15), the partition ID is appended after a tilde: urn:lex:fr:etat:loi:2004-05-15;106~art15;par3. When resolved to HTTP, this becomes a URL with a fragment identifier that points directly to the relevant section.

A resolver can handle incomplete or imprecise references by applying heuristics and normalization—expanding abbreviations, unifying institution names, and using context—similar to how a human reader would interpret a legal citation. If a document has moved, the resolver can still find it because the name is based on the document's identity, not its location.

LEX also supports language variants and local date formats. A jurisdiction using a calendar other than the Gregorian calendar can add its local date format to the LEX name (separated by a pipe, e.g., 1999-09-02|כ״א-בֶּאֱלוּל-תשנ״ט for both ISO format and Hebrew calendar), making the name intelligible to users of that jurisdiction.
sections.eli5: When a lawyer cites a law by its LEX name, a computer can automatically find it and show the reader the exact text, even if the website moves. You can cite a specific paragraph by adding it to the name, and the system will take you straight there.

sections.title: Names Must Be Simple and Stable
sections.content:
LEX names are restricted to ensure they work across all systems and languages. Reserved characters (: ; @ $ + | , ~) are used as separators and have fixed meanings. Other special characters, accents, and non-ASCII characters are normalized: spaces and connectives are replaced with dots, accented letters are converted to base ASCII equivalents (e.g., é becomes e), and non-Latin alphabets are transcribed to Latin or percent-encoded.

This ensures that:

  • LEX names can be used safely in DNS queries and HTTP URLs
  • Names are unambiguous and case-insensitive
  • International jurisdictions with non-Latin scripts can still participate
  • The names remain readable and interpretable

For example, the Icelandic term "lov" with the character restriction becomes "lov"; a French "décision" becomes "decision". These normalized forms are easier for automated systems to handle while remaining understandable to humans.
sections.eli5: LEX names must be simple so computers can handle them reliably. Accents, fancy characters and spaces are simplified into basic letters and dots, so every system in the world can read them the same way.
